<!-- The CV first screen (2026-08-16). The staircase hero used to spend the whole
     viewport on a slogan, five links and a status line: forty words about the
     author, and it read as any generated minimal site. The corners stay
     (identity top-right, status bottom-left, ledger bottom-right) but the middle
     is now CONTENT — a Now paragraph in first person, a selected-work strip, and
     a figure plate — the same move the reference sites make (Cadile's Now block,
     McCurdy's featured work): a first screen you can read like a résumé without
     clicking. This overturns the 2026-08-06 verdict that "the middle was never a
     hole"; design/direction.md 2026-08-16 records why.

     THE PLATE. "A head reads this page": the site's own headline, set as
     characters, with a head of the induction post's model — Niche, the 6-block
     character transformer — reading it left to right, its attention drawn as
     arcs. The weights are REAL and baked (assets/site/hero-plate-data.html, from
     tools/hero-plate/compute.py); no model runs in the browser, canvas only, no
     WebGL, so it is identical in every browser (cross-browser parity rule). It
     is general mech-interp imagery — attention arcs are the field's shared
     picture — pointed at something specific and true: our model, our head, our
     headline. With JS off the plate is the headline text and its caption; under
     prefers-reduced-motion the full arc field draws once, still.

     The Now paragraph is prose that goes stale. It is the one block here that
     is meant to be rewritten by hand as the work moves; the status line below
     it stays the machine-checked freshness claim.

     DOM order stays reading order: headline → identity → now/work/plate → foot;
     the identity corner is placed visually with flex `order`. Each
     .rise-mask/.rise pair is one beat of the entrance (assets/site/hero-motion.html). -->

        <!-- The status line, genuinely live (2026-08-04). The QUESTION is
             editorial and stays in the markup — it is the one sentence that
             says what I am doing right now. What JS adds is the evidence that
             it is still happening: the last push to the experiment's repo, as
             a relative stamp (assets/site/hero-status.html). Named by
             `data-repo`, so pointing the line at the next project is a
             one-attribute edit.
             The COMMIT MESSAGE is deliberately not shown — "fix seed" in a
             hero is worse than nothing; freshness is the only part of a commit
             stream a visitor can use.
             Both the stamp and the cursor ship `hidden`. The cursor's whole
             claim is "this line is live", so it may only appear once something
             live has actually landed — with JS off, rate-limited, or the repo
             gone, the line renders as the plain question it always was, and
             nothing blinks to promise otherwise. -->

     seam dims on scroll — so by the time the reader reached the list, its
     name had faded out. Labels belong to the content they label. -->

<!-- The colophon whisper (2026-08-06). /colophon/ is deliberately NOT a ledger
     row: the ledger files work, and a page about how the site is built is the
     site talking about itself. A quiet centred line under everything is the rank
     that claim deserves — and it is the exact object this rule was written for
     back when it carried a panda credit. -->

```{=html}
<!-- The ledger's honest-count guarantee: re-read each collection's size from
     the listings this same page just rendered. No fetch, no state — if JS is
     off, the publish-time numbers in the markup stand (and were true when
     written). padStart keeps the two-digit filing format the numerals share
     with the posts' section counters. -->
<script>
  document.querySelectorAll(".hero-ledger a[data-counts]").forEach(function (a) {
    var n = document.querySelectorAll("#listing-" + a.getAttribute("data-counts") + " .quarto-post").length;
    var el = a.querySelector(".ledger-n");
    if (el && n) el.textContent = String(n).padStart(2, "0");
  });
</script>
```
